title: 🏛️ Eryndor Living Culture Atlas VIII — Thrones, Eldar, Urakai, Humans & Elder Courts
rawNotionMarkup: Eryndor Living Culture Atlas VIII — creator-directed expansion, Year 3,847. Every people contains multiple cultures; every region contains multiple subcultures. Species is not a single personality, law, faith, style, family structure or destiny. The entries below are newly authored, creator-revisable cultural possibilities built on the existing Peoples, Politics and Living Atlas I–VII, not recovered original play dialogue. No birth/fertility rates, existing populations, family relationships, species abilities, established political history or in-world time are altered. Gloin has not automatically learned this information. ## Era of Fire — third and final era of the Second Age, 116 years (creator canon, 21 November 2026) AVARRAN HISTORICAL NAME, CREATOR-ESTABLISHED: The third and final Avarran-defined era of Eryndor's Second Age is called the Era of Fire; other continents may name or divide the period differently. It lasted 116 years, corresponding to Second Age Years 1,322–1,437 inclusive. Its exact duration is derived from the already confirmed Second Age total: 1,437 − 321 years (Era of Awakening) − 1,000 years (Era of Wonder) = 116 years. Chronology: (1) Era of Awakening, Years 1–321, 321 years; (2) Era of Wonder, Years 322–1,321, 1,000 years; (3) Era of Fire, Years 1,322–1,437, 116 years. The catastrophic global earthquakes at the end of the Era of Fire ended the Second Age and began the Third Age. Their causes, seismic effects, sudden marshland and lowland mountain uplift, tenfold global aftershock amplification through the ancient Ironspine, mass deaths without whole-species extinction and the as-yet-undefined magical protection are recorded separately, not invented here. CREATOR REVISION — HISTORICAL DEVELOPMENT NOW AUTHORIZED: The earlier prohibition against writing the Era of Fire's interior was superseded on 21 November 2026. Its cultures, regional kingdoms, wars, social movements and dark-mage events are now documented in the Second Age Annals and the dedicated Era of Fire chronicle. No First Throne involvement, new worldwide catastrophe, specific dragon cult or fire god is thereby established. The name Fire is an Avarran historical era name; its definitive etymology remains open. Gloin's ancestry and paused campaign remain unaffected. ## Second Age racial histories I — major peoples and elder courts (Awakening and Wonder ONLY, creator-authorized expansion, 21 November 2026) STATUS: Newly developed historical cultural lore for the Era of Awakening (Second Age Years 1–321) and Era of Wonder (Years 322–1,321). This is broad, canonically usable historical development, not an assignment of modern regimes, royals, cities, exact founding dates or events to the period. Different members, regions and families chose differently. The earlier chapter concentrated on Avarra's first two eras; the later Era of Fire is now extensively developed in the linked dedicated chronicle and the full Second Age Annals. ### Khazari — the twin duty of stone and spell Awakening: In older mountain dwellings and working caverns, spells that once measured stone stresses or kept water flowing could become misleading or cease to respond. Khazari families came to admire crews who could restore a settlement with picks, leverage, gravity-fed sluices and plain masonry even when a rune failed. A tradition remembered in later craft teaching as the Two-Hand Rule took shape: every vital enchanted work should have a physical means of inspection, repair or survival. There was no single decree, and some ambitious craft houses continued dangerously bold experiments. The original, pre-First-Age Ironspine ring itself was NOT formed during either era. Wonder: Khazari runesmiths, masons, forgebinders and Deepcraft practitioners became exceptionally skilled at combining newly understood moon-born workings with mechanical design, structural redundancy, underground farms and great waterworks. Some workshops prized remarkable enchantment; others prided themselves on quiet reliability; both could become prestigious. Apprentices learned to distinguish a truly changed spell from a poorly forged implement. Families, solitary masters and ordinary contributors all belonged to the age's prosperity. This does not establish the First Throne's existence during the Second Age or date the later Seven Thrones. ### Eldar — the living calendar and the gardens that did not sleep Awakening: In woodland regions across several continents, the collapse of familiar lunar rhythms forced Eldar stewards to stop assuming that enchanted seasons and moon-timed wards would behave as before. They cultivated ordinary seed banks, orchards, field healing and careful observations of the actual sky. The Living Calendar tradition arose in some circles: different witnesses compared what the trees, stars, water and moonlight actually did, rather than relying upon inherited ritual expectation. Some guarded the old ways, some broke ceremonially with them. None could authenticate the vanished First Age through surviving texts. Wonder: New moon-born disciplines became materials for music, living architecture, art, illumination, healing and precise woodland protections. Forest circles developed distinct approaches: patient biological research, daring public spellcraft, diplomatic grove stewardship and intensely private artistry. Long-lived individuals could pass personal observations from Awakening to Wonder, while younger generations questioned their mentors. No present-day royal dynasty or High Sovereign is automatically dated to this millennium. ### Humans — many answers to the same ruined sky Awakening: Human farmers, seafarers, healers, caravans and city communities across Eryndor faced wildly different losses. In some places ordinary mills, rain capture and hand-kept medical notes sustained the population; elsewhere ambitious elites hoarded rare working enchantments and ordinary people resisted. Ancestral human communities often remembered the Second Measure: count what a spell promises, then count what it actually delivers. No one human kingdom or government spoke for all mankind. Wonder: New spell schools proliferated in coastal ports, interior farming regions, desert river towns and northern settlements, and practical trades developed beside them. Magical irrigation, healing studies, crafted light, stage illusion and navigation were fields of experiment and mastery, not universally available conveniences. Wealth, education, household structures and faith still differed; prosperity was widespread without erasing poverty or tyranny. These are ancestral human developments and not automatic founding histories for Aldermere, Valtoria, the modern Merchant Republics, Northern Holds or Southern Sultanates. ### Drakari — keepers of the changed sky Awakening: Drakari sought to understand why the lunar powers they observed had changed. Some withdrew to watch the new sky, some bargained to protect threatened settlements and others demanded tribute for shelter. True dragons did not preserve an authenticated First Age archive merely by being ancient; a dragon's later account of those vanished times is not first-hand First Age documentary evidence. Wonder: Individual dragons and courts could become skilled interpreters of new celestial conditions, choosing whether to share, exchange or jealously guard what they learned. Treaties, philosophies of stewardship and territorial disputes evolved beside personal magical experimentation. Dragons are not all members of one school or one benevolent order; neither a global draconic empire nor an exact draconic census is added. ### Aelwyn — the price of a changing promise Awakening: Where certain lunar-supported wards or rites ceased behaving predictably, Fae courts, little households and solitary wanderers were forced to distinguish the power of a promise from the workings meant to enforce it. Some communities revised their bargain customs and shelter practices; others became more secretive or exploited bewildered outsiders. The independent World's Breath still flowed, so the Fae were not uniformly cut off from every magic. Wonder: Seasonal courts and unaligned families developed unfamiliar lunar rites of hospitality, concealment, enchantment, ceremony and dangerous reciprocity. New forms of moon magic made once-impossible effects attainable, though exact powers and specific moon affiliations remain unnamed. Concealed hamlets and public gatherings alike could flourish; Fae gifts could heal or harm, and neither cruelty nor generosity is inherent to the people. Global interpretation: The first era left a strong ethic of practical resilience; the second saw mastery of the new lunar repertoire and broad flourishing, not rediscovery of powers made impossible by destroyed moons. Mixed peoples shared knowledge, competed for access and sometimes suffered injustice. Exact rulers, battles, famous inventions, treaties and named modern institutions are deliberately not assigned here. ## The six layers of identity — use all of them 1. People/species: shared biological requirements and some historical traditions, never universal morality or occupation. 2. Continent and landscape: highlands, coast, steppe, forest, metropolis, river delta and desert each produce different needs and institutions. 3. State or locality: separate laws, taxes, public festivals, borders, languages and loyalties; seven independent Khazari Thrones are seven separate political worlds. 4. Subculture/community: urban, rural, merchant, fisher, craft, martial, scholarly, nomadic, mixed-species, diasporic, secretive, religious or irreligious networks, often overlapping. 5. Household/class: guild families, tenants, merchants, soldiers, wealthy dynasts, poor workers, adopted kin, captives and freemen experience the same city differently. 6. Individual: a person's ambitions, relationships, fears, humor, abilities, failures and choices may contradict all expectations. Cultural design test: For each group identify what earns respect, what gets criticized, its range of household models, class tensions, outsiders' stereotypes, and at least one dissenting or neighboring way of living. No species is universally enslaving, oppressed, brave, cowardly, pacifist or industrious. The existence of grimdark institutions is political and historical, not biology. ## The Khazari — seven Throne traditions, not seven species Confirmed creator principle: Family and mastery are independent. Respected lives include a supreme craft master with children, an ordinary worker with a big family, a master without a family, a person without remarkable mastery or children who still works and contributes. Deliberate capable idleness can draw social disapproval. Raising children, caring for elders, studying, recovering and community service count as contribution. Involuntary unemployment, poverty, illness and disability are not laziness. This is primarily a Khazari social expectation—do not copy it onto all peoples. | Regional Khazari subculture | What it admires | Family, customs and fault lines | | --- | --- | --- | | Stonehand Hearthworks — Karak-Varn | Reliability, practical repair, contractual integrity, ingenuity | Intergenerational workshops, large clan suppers, apprenticeships; high guilds sometimes underrate domestic labor | | Measured Stone Houses — Az-Rhumen | Accurate surveying, humble correction of mistakes, teaching | Archive-and-surveyor families, examinations and route maps; disputes over certifying poor apprentices | | Snowgate Kin — Thar-Keld | Rescue, resilience, maintaining mountain passes | Shared seasonal shelters, foster bonds between rescue crews; pressure on those who dislike hazardous field work | | Deepgarden Circles — Durn-Khaz | Food stewardship, clean water, security of supply | Multigenerational cultivation caverns and seasonal seed feasts; disputes over allocating scarce water | | Two-Tongue Gate Houses — Karak-Orun | Trustworthy trade across cultural frontiers and protection | Bilingual merchant kin, smiths and border-watch families; militarists versus conciliatory traders | | Lakeward Locksfolk — Morn-Tar | Maintaining canals, fisheries, freight and rescue equipment | Extended boat-and-pump households, annual water accounting; inheritance debts versus communal rights | | Emberward Guild Families — Vuldur-Kaz | Masterwork innovation and protecting fellow workers | Foundry households, heat-safe public works, ceremonial first-pour gatherings; output-focused owners versus safety advocates | | Roadforge Clans — foreign towns and caravans | Useful repair, language learning, mobile trust | Family caravans, adopted apprentices, trade marriages; some rooted Khazari dismiss their mobility | | Quiet Quarry Settlers — remote Ironspine hamlets | Community survival and dependable neighborliness | Village councils, small mining and farming households; old families sometimes resent arriving migrants | Distinctive generational feature: A family may include a master grandmother, a father who has only recently become a journeyman, siblings with entirely different aims, and children apprenticed in another Throne. Clan kinship is not a single occupation, and disagreements can last decades without breaking affection. Do not reassign the unresponsive three Thrones to named states without source evidence. ## Proposed southern Urakai mountain homelands overlooking the Crown Sea — creator option, 21 November 2026 Proposal, not yet a fixed surveyed geography or state name: In addition to their established Eastern Grasslands and newly confirmed major southeastern badlands/wastes populations, some Urakai orcs could occupy an extensive southern Avarran mountain range above the Crown Sea, with high cliff fortresses, defensible valley cities, terraced villages, pass-forts and long-lived clan halls. This placement is additive to existing Urakai cultural geography, not a relocation that empties the badlands or eastern plains. The mountain chain's exact name, orientation, distance from Valtoria and Sahrad, political borders and precise location on the approved Avarran map remain unsettled; do not canonize decorative map labels for it. Cultural/economic possibilities: Distinct southern mountain Urakai polities or clan confederations might control lofty passes between badlands, fertile southern foothills and the Crown Sea, earning livelihoods from stonework, metalcraft, high-valley terrace farming, quarrying, herding and coastal/transmontane trade. Lower-elevation orchards, springs, aqueducts/cisterns, guarded caravan roads, sea-facing ports or tributary markets can support permanent cities; exposed alpine peaks remain mostly sparsely settled. This allows sophisticated defenses, trade competition, civic institutions and internal disagreements rather than a universally hostile fortress race. Some settlements could be mixed with independent Ogre, Goblin, Kobold, Troll, Gnome, Minotaur, Harpy and other established peoples if ecology and local relations support them, without automatically making those peoples subordinate to Urakai. Continuity safeguards: The Avarran modeled 108m Urakai and 1,019.760m total residents already include potential southern mountain Urakai; adding this region should redistribute residents, not inflate the planetwide 6× totals. No new ruler, empire, war, attack on Valtoria, hidden First Throne revelation, Gloin action, or specific place name is canonized. The separate seven Khazari Ironspine Thrones, Veiled Inland Sea, north/south expansions, western Letharion and Shattered Gulf, and many peoples across Avarra are unaffected. ## Avarra settled western expansion and southeastern Urakai badlands — creator design (21 November 2026) Creator's governing geographical settlement direction: The thousands-of-miles-wide territory between Avarra's far western coastline and the Ironspine Mountains is populated with more of the existing elder peoples, at least two distinctive human cultural regions, and Urakai societies; it is NOT a blank forest, an entirely Eldar monopoly, or an empty ocean-to-mountain stretch. The eastern and southeastern badlands/wastes must also contain substantial established Urakai (orc) populations rather than portray all orcs only in the Eastern Grasslands or all badlands as uninhabited. Both directions complement, rather than replace, the already-established Eldar Letharion High Sovereign, southern Aldermere and Valtoria, and independent Eastern Grasslands Urakai clan cities. ### Expanded west — cultural geography (new placement directions) - Deep and northern Letharion: A very large connected forest domain with multiple Eldar houses, high-canopy courts, scholar groves, river-house settlements, independent woodland communities and protected old-growth country. The High Sovereign exists, but independent councils and houses do not share a single politics. Ent grove societies and Pixie settlements occupy some woods; Aelwyn Fae may maintain seasonal court enclaves and uncommon crossings, which are not automatically public cities or universally accessible lands. Aelwyn and Pixies are separate peoples, not interchangeable 'fairies'. Drakari might have rare remote court or sanctuary territories, but no mass dragon population or exact location is declared. Smaller peoples and mixed communities (Gnomes, Halflings, Goblins, Satyrs, Brownies and others) can be substantial and culturally distinctive. - Western and southwest river valleys and foothills: Broad fertile plains and wooded belts with distinct human river-farming and inland market-town cultures, mixed with Eldar, Gnomes, Halflings and other existing peoples. Some communities can be influenced by Aldermere without automatically becoming new Aldermere provinces. Freeholders, river-canal guilds, caravan market leagues and hereditary local lords may coexist; legal/political boundaries remain open. - Far-western outer coasts and storm-facing peninsulas: Another distinct human maritime/coastal cultural grouping, with navigators, seafaring town leagues, fortified ports, weather traditions, fishing and remote island contact. These can trade with the established Shattered Coast merchant republics without silently being those same republics, Valtorian colonies or a unified new empire. Include nonhuman merchant, crafts and shore settlements, and preserve the Shattered Gulf's indented southwestern coast. - Western uplands, dry western marches and road corridors: Urakai traders, herders, mixed frontier towns and some long-standing urban or mountain-edge communities must be present west of the Ironspine too; no premise confines the species to the east. They interact through markets, treaties, cultural mixing, competing land use and at times warfare, not merely as hostile raiders. Existing northern forests and wildlands still have vast stretches of genuinely difficult terrain. ### Southeastern wastes and badlands — settled Urakai homelands (new binding habitation direction) - Urakai are long-established peoples of multiple major southeastern badlands/wastes communities since their creation sometime in the Third Age; the subsequent history of specific clans and their migrations remains open. Their presence cannot predate the Third Age. They are not just occasional invaders or temporary caravans from the eastern plains. Show recognisable permanent cities/fortified towns in canyon basins, near spring-fed rivers, protected oases and volcanic/mesa foothills, plus distributed hamlets, mine towns, road stations and migrating pastoral/clan groups. Strong enough local political institutions for law, trade, sophisticated craft, engineering, agriculture and military history. - Possible regional cultures, proposed descriptive labels not confirmed state names: canyon-basin waterwardens (reservoir builders, collective cistern laws, terrace farms), ash-ridge foundry clans (ore, ceramic craft, sophisticated metalwork and severe heat safety), salt-road caravan confederations (wells, navigation, trader treaties, mobile households), and dry-grassland edge settlements (pastoral and farm links to the Eastern Grasslands). These societies can have different dialects, governments, faiths, classes, attitudes toward outsiders and rivalries; a single 'badlands orc king' or automatic warlord state is NOT canon. - Resource/carrying capacity: Most scorched and dry interior terrain remains sparse or physically uninhabited; the substantial Urakai numbers concentrate around perennial springs, river corridors, aquifers, cistern chains, crop terraces, quarry/mineral trade, livestock routes and coastal trade access. Canals, runic/ordinary engineering, storage and imports help support larger cities but cannot erase drought, conflict or bad harvests. Populations and city sizes must be determined as nested shares of the existing numerical continent/people allocation rather than added to it. - Relations: Urakai communities of the southeastern badlands and adjoining eastern frontier can be related or competing cultures, with migration, treaty roads and trade linking the grasslands, Ironspine east/southeast foothills and far southern regions. Some populations also interact with Valtoria and local mixed peoples. No Urakai people or Urakai-specific magic is intrinsically evil on account of ancestry; actual moral character belongs to individual actions and particular magical forces. ### Demographic, religious and cartographic guardrails Under the creator's sixfold demographic model, Avarra has 1,019.760 million modeled residents, including 108 million Avarran Urakai, 72 million Avarran Eldar, and 468 million Avarran humans. The new western and southeastern communities are distributions within these already-counted figures, not extra populations added to the continental total. Aelwyn remain uncensused in the 28-people numerical matrix; do not manufacture a precise Fae census. The settlements need many thousands of miles of viable trade, farmland and transport corridors, but climate, rocky uplands, river access and wilderness create strong settlement differences. Preserve birth rates and long-lived family dynamics. Dwarven chart requirements: On an updated private Khazari map, extend the far west with named Letharion Forest, ancient Eldar centers, Ent/Fae enclaves and smaller-peoples' woodland towns; mark two human culture belts (inland agrarian river/market societies and far-west maritime/port societies), plus some western Urakai settlements along uplands and roads. Mark several Urakai settlement clusters and substantial cities inside the southeastern badlands and wastes with trade roads following water and canyon routes. Do not move the seven Ironspine Thrones, expose the hidden Veiled Inland Sea to public maps, erase the Shattered Gulf, or replace established cultures and city names with AI-invented sovereign states. No unapproved proper names, dates, scale bars or arbitrary city population labels become canon from the illustration. In-world Gloin has not acquired an omniscient survey merely because we design one out-of-character. ## Eldar — no single “elven culture” Established basis: Letharion's royal houses and High Sovereign, ancient forest traditions, long lives, formal etiquette, scholarship, diplomacy, aesthetic and historical pursuits. Many forms of family, marriage, child-rearing, mastery or solitude are possible. No new fertility assumptions. | Eldar subculture | Values and respected paths | Tensions and local behavior | | --- | --- | --- | | High Canopy Courts — Letharion | Elegance, court diplomacy, genealogical memory, precise promises | Court patronage can exclude blunt outsiders or humble foresters | | Silverflow Riverhouses — southern Letharion | Bargemen, orchard tending, medicine, woodworking, mixed trade | River tolls and timber-right disputes mean practical work trumps courtly fashion | | Greenwarden Groves — Vaelora Elderwood | Generational stewardship, tree lore, coexistence with Ent councils | Local conservation law may clash with migrant settlements | | Opal Coast Scholars — Orundel / Sahrad enclaves | Botany, language exchange, field observation, patient research | Diaspora families debate ancestral custom versus integration | | Free Branch Artisans — port and frontier quarters | Public art, street craft, irreverence, experimental architecture | Some regard formal High Court traditions as a burden | | Remembrance Keepers — dispersed houses | Honoring the living and lost, mediation, preservation of artifacts | A long memory can aid reconciliation or sustain devastating feuds | Family and class: Loving multigenerational homes, fosterage, chosen kin and independent solitary artists coexist. An Eldar parent can be a great historical scholar, a humble gardener, a sailor or an unemployed noble. Disapproval varies: falsifying a respected record may be worse in archive circles than skipping a formal dance; destroying a grove is especially grave to Greenwardens. Some individuals are brilliant, selfish, generous, contemptuous or funny—none by species command. ## Eastern/western Urakai placement correction — explicit creator decision (21 November 2026) Binding cartographic correction superseding earlier atlas descriptions: Urakai are a rising power in the eastern and southeastern badlands/wastes of Avarra, and may also have substantial fortified homelands in the southern mountains overlooking the Crown Sea. They are extremely rare in the Eastern Grasslands, with NO established Urakai settlements there. Avarra's far west is NOT a principal centre of Urakai political rise and must not be illustrated as another large Urakai homeland; western territory is centered on Eldar and other elder peoples, multiple human cultural zones, widespread Goblins and Ogres, and other previously established peoples. Lone Urakai travellers, merchants and unusual diaspora individuals do not make a settled western population or permanent eastern-grassland state. This corrects the older notes that placed major Urakai clan capitals and cities in the Eastern Grasslands or prescribed western Urakai towns as mandatory. Named settlement continuity: Preserve established names Khurazh, Rakh-Dor, Vesk Plain, Old Seven Wells, and Rider's Truce and their revised 6× population reference values. Former geographic attribution of Urakai cities in the Eastern Grasslands is superseded; their exact new locations belong to the southeastern badlands / eastern frontier or southern Crown Sea mountain approaches, as appropriate in a later measured atlas. Do not place established Urakai towns in the Eastern Grasslands. Non-Urakai Centaur, Goblin, Kobold, Cowfolk/Pigfolk and Harpy settlements from the earlier Eastern Grasslands gazetteer may continue there unless a later decision moves them. The prior section and source grid are historical drafts, not current coordinates. Avarra's modeled 108 million Urakai remains unchanged; this is a redistribution of where they live, not a demographic increase, overnight migration or in-story war. An unnamed rising warlord remains a rumor/plot lead; nothing identifies or mandates him as their universal leader. ## Why Goblins, Ogres and Urakai face western prejudice — older war history (21 November 2026) Creator's historical explanation: During wars between eastern and western peoples in the Third Age or later, some eastern Goblin and Ogre groups fought with or aided Urakai. Long after Goblins and Ogres moved into western lands and established ordinary, numerous communities, memory of those alliances persisted as discrimination. Western Goblins are stereotyped as thieving/conniving and widely distrusted; Ogres are widely feared, in part due to fearsome wartime reputation; rare western Urakai visitors face antipathy tied to their eastern political and military associations. These are historically inherited prejudices, not innate racial traits or proof all ancestral groups took one side. Exact dates, war names, cultures and campaigns are OPEN. The creator also raised eastern origins and the possibility that Goblins/Ogres are distinct distant biological cousins of Urakai; biological kinship is NOT established. Eastern/southeastern badlands are the main current Urakai heartlands; the Eastern Grasslands have very rare Urakai and no established Urakai settlements. Western Goblins/Ogres remain commonplace. See 03 — History & Ancient Lore for the full historical and canon-status distinction. ## Urakai / Orcs — FIRST APPEAR IN THE THIRD AGE, absent from First and Second Ages (binding creator correction, 21 November 2026) CANON CHRONOLOGICAL RULE — supersedes conflicting earlier text: Urakai (Orcs) did not exist in the First Age or anywhere in the 1,437-year Second Age. The exiled dark mages of southeastern Avarra created the Orcs sometime during the Third Age. The exact Third Age year, creation method, first location, identities of the first communities, and subsequent structure of mage–Orc command remain UNDECIDED. The Orcs were absent from the Second Age's Era of Awakening (Years 1–321), Era of Wonder (Years 322–1,321) and Era of Fire (Years 1,322–1,437). Earlier lore depicting Orc inhabitants, clans, armies, cities or events in either of those two Ages is superseded and noncanon. Goblins and Ogres may predate the Third Age. CREATOR CANON — Third Age creation and intended conquests: The exiled dark mages who formed the southeastern Avarran Southern Wastes and its volcano during the Second Age survived well into the Third Age, when they created the Urakai (Orcs) by a method not yet decided. Their ambition in creating the Orcs was first to besiege the dwarven (Khazari) strongholds, and ultimately to attack the Eldar and human kingdoms. This establishes the mages' intentions, not any particular siege, conquest, campaign, chronology, victory or attack as an accomplished fact. The mages established no diplomacy, trade, treaties or alliances with pre-existing outside peoples; creating the Orcs is an act of creation for the mages' ambitions, not evidence of diplomatic relations. The exact magical or other creation process, timing, first Orc settlements, degree and duration of mage control, and later independence or resistance remain open. The modern Urakai are a diverse people with their own cultures and agency; they are not collectively evil, personally culpable for the mages' acts, or necessarily still subject to their creators. Effects on war histories: Any established older east–west wars involving Urakai, and any historical Goblin/Ogre alliances or assistance with Orc forces, must have happened in the Third Age or later, with no specific Age within that range, reign, battle, migration date or formal state assigned yet. The anti-Goblin, anti-Ogre and anti-Urakai prejudices of western Avarra remain valid consequences of those undated wars. These cannot predate the Third Age. Nor should living Urakai's settled southeast badlands homelands and their modern peoples/cultures be erased or treated as magically evil due to a speculative ancient link. Canon controls and campaign: Modern Urakai exist in large numbers, with sophisticated diverse societies, independent cities, families, economies, politics, culture and varied morality. Existing Fifth Age maps and sixfold census are unchanged; this corrects only their ancestral chronology. No changes to family rates, species lifespans or present demographics. The no-species-extinction rule at the Second Age-ending earthquake stays: Urakai were not a species that survived that disaster, because they had not appeared yet; all peoples existing at that time survived somewhere. Do not connect their origin to Gloin Hammerfeld's genuinely unknown genealogy, the First Throne, the lost First Age moon-magics or the yet-unexplained global species-survival magical force without an explicit new creator decision. ## Dark mages and the Urakai (Orcs) — CREATION CONFIRMED IN THIRD AGE; MILITARY AMBITIONS ESTABLISHED (creator canon, 21 November 2026) CREATOR'S BINDING THIRD AGE HISTORY: The exiled dark mages of southeastern Avarra created the Orcs sometime in the Third Age in pursuit of a planned war of conquest: besiege the Khazari dwarven strongholds first, then eventually attack the Eldar and human kingdoms. This was an ambition and intended sequence, not confirmation that specific attacks or wars actually took place. Their creation technique, timing, organization of the first Orcs, later relationship to the mages, and historical results are intentionally not yet defined. The Orcs were wholly absent from the First and Second Ages. Existing binding facts: At the beginning of the Era of Fire (Second Age Year 1,322), exiled mages created the southeastern Avarran wastes and their volcano using dark magic. At the close of the Second Age (Year 1,437), the global earthquakes intensified that volcano; the mages harnessed its energy to reduce volcanic devastation and unwittingly gained greater magical strength. The mages survived well into the Third Age and established NO relations with any outside peoples—no alliances, trade, diplomacy or cooperative ties. Modern southeastern Avarra includes substantial independent Urakai communities. Urakai are not universally evil, dark mages or participants in the mages' deliberate destruction by default. Open questions, NOT decided: By what magical or other means the dark mages created the first Orcs; the precise year and place within the Third Age; whether each mage participated or held equal authority; the numbers, first communities and abilities of created Orcs; whether and how the creators commanded them; whether the intended sieges and later attacks occurred, against which named strongholds or kingdoms, with what resistance and outcomes; and the emergence of independent Orc cultures over later generations. Do not fill these gaps automatically. The mages' earlier political and diplomatic isolation from existing outside peoples still stands: no unapproved treaties, trade, alliances or diplomatic partners. Present-day Urakai are distinct individuals and societies, not automatically loyal to ancient mages. Protected mysteries: Exact races/identities of the original mage groups are still unknown; the mages' ancestry and ultimate fate are open. No link to the First Throne, historical east–west wars, the original lunar catastrophe, or Gloin Hammerfeld's genuinely unpredetermined heritage is proved. Leave this thread available for later creator decisions without resolving it during campaign play or by editorial inference. ## Urakai — clan variation, urban sophistication and different ideals Established basis: Industrious, technologically sophisticated Urakai with cities, universities, military schools, agriculture and political factions. Clan ties, courage, achievement and directness are prominent reputations, not universal laws. The report of a rising unidentified warlord remains unresolved, and his actions are not assumed. | Urakai subculture | Respected paths and family life | Political/social friction | | --- | --- | --- | | Khurazh Assembly Clans — eastern/southeastern Avarran badlands; former grassland placement superseded | Public argument, leadership, skilled teaching, law and clan trust | Competing clan votes, scholarly disputation, urban hierarchy | | Grassroad Herd Houses — dry badlands fringes and southern mountain foothills; no established Urakai settlements in Eastern Grasslands | Stewarding herds and wells, riding, hospitality, protecting caravan routes | Pasture rights and Centaur treaties versus expansionist farmers | | Rakh-Dor River Guilds — river cities | Irrigation engineering, grain accounting, smithing, barges | Taxes and central planning versus small traders and rural clan leaders | | Emberback Foundry Circles — Orundel | Metallurgy, design, workshop safety, industrial rivalry | Engineers clash with warlords and mine owners | | Tharvorn Border Hearths — northern settlements | Winter mutual aid, kin rescue, sheltering strangers during storms | Distance from old clan courts and mixed-marriage customs | | Wayfarer Oath-Circles — diaspora | Keeping trade agreements, acting as translators, mercenary professionalism | Branded outsiders by some hardliners; travelers criticize clan exclusivity | | Red Banner War Houses — limited hostile political factions | Victory, conquest, ransom, warrior status | Can glorify enslavement and raids; opposed by other Urakai councils and kin groups | Family and respect: Large clan reunions, adoptive kin, mentors and comrades may form overlapping loyalties. A peaceful parent, veteran, engineer, dancer, agronomist or barrister can earn admiration. War-captive practices differ by polity, not ancestry. A cruel Urakai slaver, compassionate Urakai judge and indecisive Urakai merchant are all believable individuals. ## Humans — five political-cultural umbrellas with real internal diversity Human regional identity is civic, linguistic, historical and political, not biological. These subcultures describe major civic traditions while leaving room for local variations in every city, village and hamlet. ## Other elders: Drakari and Aelwyn — courts are not identical ### Drakari, living True Dragons - Oathfire Courts: Value literal treaty performance, reputation across centuries and defending territorial bonds; a quiet treaty-keeper can be more respected than a conqueror. - Ember Crown Dynasts: Value power, sovereignty, ancestral claims and monumental building; family politics and inheritance can be fierce. - Skyroad Observers: Prize aerial exploration, celestial research, philosophy and knowledge rather than treasure. - Solitary Vale-Keepers: Seek privacy, territory and long personal projects; kin ties may be close even when contact is rare. - Uncertainties: Exact draconic families, mating, population (\<10k estimate), longevity and court membership remain canonically underdefined; no new reproductive rules are being established. These are proposed traditions, not four dragon subspecies. ### Aelwyn, Fair Folk - Spring Invitation Courts: Gifts, hospitality, promises of renewal and the precise interpretation of invitation. - High Summer Revel Houses: Performance, public prestige, feast debts and the privileges of hosts; not all members are frivolous. - Autumn Bargain Guilds: Contract symbolism, reciprocal exchanges, names and consequences of broken promises. - Winter Silence Circles: Privacy, secrecy, memory, old obligations and endurance across long absences. - Unaligned Hollow Walkers: Small households, wanderers and solitary individuals rejecting seasonal court hierarchy. - Uncertainties: “Seasonal” labels reflect existing courts, not proof they are biologically four different kinds of Fae. Their relation to real-world seasons, reproduction, longevity, dimensional borders and exact geographic territories remain open. Customs can be strange and dangerous; not every Aelwyn is deceitful. ## Shared family and social principles — protected from retcon - Large and extended families remain alive across Eryndor, including the confirmed Hammerfeld family and its Day 21 gathering. No mass childlessness. - Long-lived people can pursue centuries-long mastery and marry, raise children, care for elders, or change priorities. Not having children is another valid personal path. - No change to birth rates, reproductive biology, sex ratios, family counts, lifespans or population tables. Nothing about one culture dictates another's biological fertility. - Any culture's ideals may be embraced, satirized, contested or exploited; a local official's rhetoric is not evidence about all of their people. - Do not reveal unrecovered lore to Gloin.
